newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany - use existing EMU coordination plans first.
newsitem.headline: Germany - use existing EMU coordination plans first.

text.p: Existing instruments to coordinate European Economic and Monetary Union need to be implemented before any new mechanisms are introduced, the German government's annual government economic report said on Monday.
The need for greater coordination between European Union members would increase before the scheduled kick-off for currency union in 1999, the report said in a draft copy obtained by Reuters.
However, it added: "Priority should be given to effective implementation of existing instruments to ensure coordination, before new mechanisms are introduced."

The comments in the report came in response to a French proposal to introduce a council to monitor the development of stability and growth, which would also examine any problems arising from meeting convergence.

In the Monday edition of the German newspaper Handelsblatt, German state secretary for finance, Juergen Stark, said the council would be an informal advisory arrangement, where the EU's finance ministers, ECOFIN, could discuss issues of convergence.
Stark went on to say that there was no need to formalise the council's activities.
The report is due to be reviewed by Chancellor Helmut Kohl's cabinet on Tuesday and was written by experts in Guenter Rexrodt's Economics Ministry.
